provenance.generator: tests/fixtures/context-source/generate_exchanges.py (imports the pinned host's context_source_status_capture and support modules)
limitations: Isolated synthetic composition, not installed-product proof: a running server, TLS, session cookies, the installed runtime lifetime wiring and the pinned dependency set are not exercised, and the host's recorded dependency pins differ from the Operations and Context commits above that this fixture ran against.

transport http-dispatcher: the request went through the real HTTPAPI dispatcher (origin/CSRF/JSON checks, operation dispatch, option splitting, selector refusal, compatibility routes, failure mapping) with the real single-owner principal resolution and a synthetic in-process Starlette request. The only faked parts are the socket and an unused signing key.

transport application-invoke: an agent principal calling Application.invoke directly. The HTTP layer's agent session resolution is not run; these entries are not HTTP evidence and show the operation result as the operation returns it. transport route-handler: a retained compatibility route handler called directly for an agent principal, errors mapped with the HTTP layer's own failure().
The model is an injected runner; no provider, native session, migration or operational data is involved. The identity and role sources are synthetic test copies.

The queue's and the background executor's clock is injected and starts at 2026-01-01T12:00:00Z, advancing only by explicit steps; those timestamps appear verbatim. Every other timestamp comes from the wall clock and is remapped onto a synthetic ordered timeline (2026-01-01T00:00:00Z plus one second per distinct instant, instants within 10 ms of each other sharing one value). Comparisons between the two time domains are not meaningful.

Entropy is deterministic during generation (os.urandom is a counter-keyed hash stream), so UUIDs are real version 4 values that are stable between runs and the id-ordered list/search pages are reproducible. The Context's five-character event and source tokens, content hashes, commit ids and ETags are replaced by stable synthetic values of the same shape in order of first appearance.

Opaque cursors are decoded, normalized and re-encoded with the library's own encoder so every request cursor still equals the response cursor it came from. A normalized cursor is therefore not valid against a live host.
The full business Context view is recorded as its keys plus its context_queue object only.

normalization.commit: 40-hex git ids -> synthetic ids of the same shape
normalization.context token: the Context's random five-character ids: values of *event_id keys -> ev001, ev002, ...; five-character source_id values -> so001, so002, ...
normalization.cursor: values of cursor, next_cursor and refresh_cursor keys: decoded, inner values normalized, re-encoded
normalization.etag: W/"<32 hex>" -> synthetic tags of the same shape
normalization.hash: sha256 digests (bare or sha256: prefixed) -> synthetic digests of the same shape
normalization.time: wall-clock instants -> 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z + cluster index seconds, original format kept; injected-clock instants (2026-01-01T12:00:00Z + advances) unchanged

provenance.what: The requests this dashboard actually sends (6000-character pages, 100-character preflights, limit 30 and 25), answered by the fixed host through its real HTTPAPI dispatcher over the host's composed synthetic test host with an injected model runner. Each exchange belongs to a named stage = one host state; responses are never edited to match another request.
